Engineer here, based on the parts list diagram provided by the other poster, it's the little L-shaped steel pin in this CZ 83 disassembly video. https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=1702&v=Yv31Mr1XLsE&feature=emb_logo

If you don't feel comfortable just having someone mail you one, this could easily be fabricated. (Moreso than pretty much everything else on this gun) Go to the hardware store and find a piece of fairly stiff wire. (stiffer wire is better). Unless you have a caliper handy to measure the diameter of the hole this pin goes into, the wire will need be ~1mm thick or so. (I don't think it's smaller, but check the holes if you can) Cut a piece thats 3-4cm long (or whatever the distance is between the two holes in this video, since you can check the firearm directly). Then bend it into shape on both ends using the pliers. ~0.5cm on the far end bent at 90 degrees, ~0.5cm on the other side bent the same direction as the 'L' but at ~10 degrees.

Depending on the wire used, I won't guarantee that it's going to last forever, but it should be fine for a couple hundred or thousand rounds-- or enough to dump a mag into someone's chest if you had to. Hell you may be able to just take a little 1mm hex wrench and cut it down to fit, bend the tail, and pop it in if its the right size for the hole.

Obviously once it's in there, check the function of the gun. If you can work it a couple dozen times without malfunction, you're good to go. Let me know if you still have issues with this.

u/Xantha is correct, this is an easily fabricated part. The wire should be "piano" or "music" wire. It is high-carbon steel and can be hardened and tempered which that part needs. You can temper wire with a candle. The wire is so small the candle produces enough heat for the job.
